goals.title: Select the relevant inventory
goals.concept: The inventory type and time range decide which entities you can fairly compare.
goals.narration: Show the inventory at the entity level that owns the reported resource.
goals.reasoning: The right entity level keeps host, container and service signals from getting mixed up.
goals.evidence: The inventory shows this incident's entities.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the ${var.inventory} inventory so we're comparing the same kind of entity when looking for an outlier.
demonstration.reasoning: Hosts, pods, containers and services are different levels. Comparing entities of the same kind gives us a fair baseline.
demonstration.evidence: The inventory now lists entities of the same kind, at the ${var.inventory} level. Next, we can look for an outlier.

hints: Choose the entity level that owns the reported resource.
Use the Infrastructure inventory's Show selector.
Select ${var.inventory}; Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Show the metric behind the problem
goals.concept: Colouring every entity by one metric makes an outlier stand out from the others.
goals.narration: Colour the inventory by the resource metric that matches the reported problem.
goals.reasoning: An overall health average can hide one saturated entity; one metric across all of them shows it.
goals.evidence: Every entity is now coloured by the chosen metric.

demonstration.narration: I'll colour the inventory by ${var.metric}, the resource that matches the reported problem, so an outlier stands out.
demonstration.reasoning: An overall health average can hide one saturated entity: one working at its limit. Showing one metric for every entity makes the comparison direct.
demonstration.evidence: Every entity is now coloured by ${var.metric}. The highlighted ${var.entity} reads far above the others, so that's the one to open next.

drifts.note: You chose ${action.value}; check whether that resource is the one the report describes.

hints: Match the metric to the problem in the brief.
Select ${var.metric}; Show me can point to it.

goals.title: Select the entity that stands out
goals.concept: Comparing similar entities shows the outlier that overall health hides.
goals.narration: Select the entity that stands apart from the others on that metric.
goals.reasoning: Compare the unusual entity with healthy ones, or with an earlier period.
goals.evidence: The selected entity's detail shows the metric that stood out.

demonstration.narration: I'll select the entity that stands apart from the others to open its detail.
demonstration.reasoning: One entity's colour isn't proof yet; its detail shows the metric over time against the incident window.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted reading is why ${truth.finding} stands apart from the others on ${var.metric}. Treat it as a guess until another signal backs up its timing.

hints: Compare the entities' colours: one should stand apart.
Click the entity in the inventory to open its detail.
Select ${var.entity}; Show me can point to it.

drifts.note: You selected ${action.value}; check whether it really stands apart from the others.

goals.title: Correlate with another signal
goals.concept: Correlation means checking that two signals change at the same time. A resource pattern means more when it lines up with a restart, a log or a latency rise.
goals.narration: Correlation means checking that two signals change at the same time. Open more metric detail, or the correlated logs from the same time.
goals.reasoning: Correlation checks that the resource pattern and the impact happen at the same time.
goals.evidence: The record backs up the finding.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the outlier's logs to see whether the resource change lines up with the reported issue.
demonstration.reasoning: A resource spike alone doesn't prove that customers were affected, or what caused it. Correlation tests the link: does another signal for the same entity change at the same time?

hints: Check whether the timing matches another signal you can see.
In the entity's detail flyout, open its Logs tab.
Open the correlated logs; Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Submit a conclusion the metrics back up
goals.concept: Say which entity, what pattern, and how the timing lines up. Don't suggest a fix.
goals.narration: Record the conclusion and supporting evidence.
goals.reasoning: This scenario tests reading Kibana, not running infrastructure.
goals.evidence: The answer points to the metric and the correlation.
